llm_findings: Single bounded treatment: enable --batch-ramp, including its existing coupled LR scaling. Authoritative train.py lines 254–270 and 6197–6212 describe fixed micro-shapes, wall-clock boundaries, accumulation (2,4,8), and LR exponent 0.5; both pinned control ledger rows confirm the same resolved defaults with the ramp disabled.

Repository-backed matched controls are available: trn21 records 2071 steps and 1.005734 public BPB; trn22 records 2076 steps and 1.005967. The predeclared same-host BPB delta and update-count criteria are falsifiable under the controller-pinned seed-42 full-chip experiment.

No closed batch-ramp direction appears in the supplied decision log or ledger excerpts. Static batch-size losses cited in train.py lines 222–237 are relevant negative evidence, but do not duplicate a time-varying batch/LR schedule. The cited BF16 experiments also use a distinct mechanism.

Competition-legal scope: README.md permits batch-size and training-schedule changes. This flag-only proposal introduces no pretrained weights, external data, evaluator changes, or modifications to protected files.

Interpretation caveats: total tokens are an outcome, not an invariant under a fixed time budget. The illustrative phase counts imply 7800 micro-batches, about 5.8–6.1% below the controls, slightly outside the stated 5% prediction. Report actual accumulated tokens and phase timings separately from BPB success. The two-host 0.000233 BPB spread is descriptive, not an established statistical noise band.
